gaps.title: Crépuscule (from Poème pastoral) (arr. Powell)
gaps.arranger: Maud Powell (IMSLP also credits Adolf Paul)
gaps.edition: New York: E. Schuberth & Co., 1892, plate E.S. & Co. 2487 (IMSLP); Powell also recorded it as 'Twilight' for Victor (matrix C-14995, Victor 74408, 1914; accompaniment on that disc reported as harp) and Rachel Barton Pine recorded it with piano on Cedille 'American Virtuosa' (c. 2:20)
gaps.note: Crépuscule (text Armand Silvestre, DO 171) is the 'Deuxième Intermède' (no. 5) of the Poème pastoral for voice, female chorus and piano (1870-72). Powell's own arrangement is dated 1891 in the Cedille booklet, 1892 on the Schuberth print. A Heugel arrangement for flute, violin, cello and strings (c. 1891) also exists but is an ensemble piece, not reported.

gaps.title: Le dernier sommeil de la Vierge (from La Vierge) (arr. Herman)
gaps.scoring: violin and piano (Saenger's Carl Fischer edition says 'or organ')
gaps.edition: Herman arr.: C. E. Music Publishers, n.d.; also New York: Carl Fischer, c. 1920, ed. Gustav Saenger, in 'Religious Meditations for Violin and Piano (or Organ)' (both per IMSLP)
gaps.note: Prelude to Scene IV of the sacred legend La Vierge (1877-78). LOWER CONFIDENCE: published violin editions confirmed on IMSLP, but arranger Herman is minor and I did not confirm a violin recording; include only if the owner wants it.

existing_issues.issue: Title misspells the source ('erinnyes' should be 'Les Érinnyes', Leconte de Lisle's play with Massenet's incidental music, 1873). The tune is the Mélodie, no. 5 of 10 Pièces de genre, Op. 10 (piano), which IMSLP says became the 'Invocation' (Act II) of Les Érinnyes and the song/violin piece 'Élégie' ('Ô doux printemps d'autrefois', DO 183, text Louis Gallet); violinists almost always call it 'Élégie'. It is one piece, so I did NOT add 'Élégie' as a gap (it would be a second version of the same piece). Violin editions exist: cello-or-violin and piano edition transcribed by Massenet (E. Fromont reprint of Girod, plate E. 2391-92 F.), Schott pl. 27828, PWM 'Violin Miniatures'; early violin recording by Erna Rubinstein (Edison, 1928).
existing_issues.suggested_title: Élégie (Mélodie, Op. 10 No. 5; Invocation, from Les Érinnyes)

gap_check_note: Gap check (sources: en Wikipedia work list, IMSLP pages for Thaïs, Élégie, Les Érinnyes, 10 Pièces de genre Op. 10, Poème pastoral, La Vierge, plus retailer/library search results): no further violin transcription by a notable violinist found for Manon, Werther, Le Cid, Le Jongleur de Notre-Dame, Hérodiade. The Méditation from Thaïs (Marsick arr. is the standard violin-and-piano edition; also violin, harp & strings by others) is already listed as id 1084. Not reported: 'Adagio religioso' for violin and organ (1867), which appears only in the Wikipedia work list with no edition found. Massenet wrote no violin concerto or sonata. WebSearch quota ran out shortly after this composer, so checks beyond these pages were not possible.
